Yesterday's numbers tell a clear story of low activity and compromised recovery. With just 4,248 steps, no training sessions, and only 5.6 hours of sleep, your body was running on minimal fuel. The bright spot? Your stress stayed remarkably low at 21/100, showing you're not carrying psychological load even when physically underperforming.

Your recovery markers paint a mixed picture right now. HRV at 98ms sits right at your baseline floor — functional but not optimal. Resting heart rate of 47 bpm looks solid, but your TSB of -17 confirms you're carrying moderate fatigue. Your fitness is building (CTL 42) while fatigue remains elevated (ATL 59), which is typical for early training phases.

Today's approach should be conservative and controlled. You're in Phase 1 where building aerobic base trumps intensity every time. If you have a run planned, keep it conversational and focus on time on feet rather than pace. Your body's telling you it needs steady, measured stress — not heroics.

Sleep debt is your enemy right now, Karl. Champions aren't built in single workouts but through consistent recovery cycles. Tonight, prioritize 7+ hours of quality sleep. Your marathon dreams live in those recovery hours, not just the running miles.
